main.description: A flair definition — a badge any account (person, org, agent) may issue. Lives in the ISSUER's repo; the record key is a lowercase slug matching [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63} chosen at creation and referenced by grants and badges. The issuer's account is the counterpart of every wear: policy 'open' is a standing consent (anyone may wear it), policy 'granted' requires a matching at.tessera.flair.grant per wearer.

policy.description: open = this definition itself authorizes anyone to wear the flair; granted = only wearers with a matching at.tessera.flair.grant in this repo. Consumers MUST fail closed on any other value.

criteria.description: Human-readable rules for earning this flair. Enforced by the issuer (who writes the grants), never by the protocol — the grant is the proof the rules were met.

style.description: Curated presentation of the badge — see #style. A ref rather than an inline object: the PDS fork's lexicon compiler only accepts objects as defs, and inline would keep these records forever unvalidatable server-side.

image.description: The badge artwork — the medallion's face. Free content on wearers' profiles, therefore consent-bound like name: consumers MUST treat any mismatch between this blob's CID and the wearer's badge.image (including one-sided absence) as not-a-wear.

style.description: Curated presentation of the badge. All values are open sets the clients curate; consumers MUST fall back to their defaults on unknown values. Presentation only — deliberately NOT consent-bound (unlike name): a restyle within the curated sets is a logo update, not a new statement.

shape.description: Medallion geometry, in the Tessera chamfer language. band is legacy and renders as mark.

tone.description: Edge and tint family: gold (default) or one of the four equal-lightness suit accents.

icon.description: Icon name from the client's curated set; unknown names render no icon.
